title: What does AccountDelete do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of AccountDelete and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, AccountDelete removes an eligible XRPL account and sends its remaining XRP to a destination account. [1]

Deletion has prerequisites involving account history and owned objects; merely spending down the balance does not delete an account. The destination must already exist. Check the reference's special transaction cost and any destination tag before signing: the normal Payment fee is not the deletion fee. [1]

The AccountDelete reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using AccountDelete, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
